• SQL: add the function road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields which adds to a managed object table the reference fields corresponding to its geometry type (migration upgrade_to_39.sql)

  • SQL: add the functions road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track which snaps an imprecise GPS track (for example from a GPX file) on the road graph edges, without zigzags between close roads, and road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line which returns the ordered list of the roads followed by the snapped line, with their start and end references (migration upgrade_to_34.sql)

  • Docs: explain the use of the field no_intersection_cutting in the page Road graph editing

docs.text:
• Docs: reorganization and new content of the documentation: new pages Processing algorithms and Tables and fields, description of the toolbar and panels of the plugin, examples of the linear referencing functions, creation of a demo database, example of the impacts of a graph modification on the business data, the preparation of the business tables moved to the page Managed objects, and a training plan in appendix

  • QGIS project: the Python code of the layer actions has been moved into the plugin (module roadnetwork/actions). The actions of the administration project now only call plugins['roadnetwork'].run_action(...): finalize_roundabout (layer edges copie), display_edited_data, create_editing_session and drop_editing_session (layer editing_sessions)

  • Processing: remove the Schema name parameter from the algorithms Create database structure and Upgrade database structure: the plugin schema is always road_graph
  • SQL: rename the editing schema editing_session to road_graph_editing (migration upgrade_to_32.sql). The table road_graph.editing_sessions and the functions *_editing_session* keep their names. The QGIS administration project and the plugin tools use the new schema name: QGIS projects created before must be recreated with the algorithm Create database local interface, or their data sources updated

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• QGIS: in the panel RoadNetwork tools, pressing Enter in a field did not run the search Find
  • QGIS: the error message of the tool Get references under the cursor raised an error itself

  • Processing: the help of the algorithm Merge editing session data was the help of the algorithm cloning the data

  • SQL: the geometry of an editing session which status is not created could still be modified by setting its status back to created in the same query, or by removing it (migration upgrade_to_38.sql)

  • Lizmap: in the references form of the road network panel, the button Road of the start references went to the end of the road instead of its start
  • SQL: split of a managed object linestring by a point (Lizmap action split_line_by_point): the references were not updated when the table has no trigger calculating them. The first part now ends, and the second part starts, at the references of the cut point. A feature digitized in the opposite direction of the road can now also be split (migration upgrade_to_37.sql)
  • SQL: drawing an edge across edges crossing without node (bridges, highway interchanges) never ended: the parts of each split edge created nodes at all their intersections, which were propagated to the edges crossing them, and so on. Only the intersections of the drawn edge are now cut
  • SQL: when a new edge crossed several edges, a second node, not linked to any edge, could be created 10 cm away from a crossing node (rounding of the coordinates of the split parts)
  • SQL: the edges with no_intersection_cutting set to True were still cut by the nodes located on them, for example a new edge with this value passing over an existing crossroad. They are now only cut when the start or end point of a created or moved edge is located on them, for example a new access road arriving in the middle of a highway edge (migration upgrade_to_36.sql)
  • SQL: performance of the references calculation: the recalculation of the edges references of all the roads (update_edge_references) is about 9 times faster, with the same results. With the road cache, the previous marker is only searched among the markers of the road (all the markers of the database were read), and the edge order is stored in the cache instead of being calculated again for each point
  • SQL: performance of the update of the managed objects references (update_table_references_from_geometries), about 3.5 times faster on long roads: the road cache can now contain several roads, and is built for the roads of the objects before calculating their references
  • SQL: get_ordered_edges returned twice the edge of the roads having only one edge
  • SQL: when the first edge of a road is updated, for example when it is split by a new node, do not create a marker 0 if the road already has markers. Some roads do not start with the marker 0 (e.g. a road starting at the marker 4 + 918): a wrong marker 0 was created, or the editing failed with the error The object geometry must intersect the editing session polygon if the start of the road was outside the editing session (migration upgrade_to_33.sql)
  • SQL: the session variables road.graph.* used by the topology triggers are set with SET LOCAL, so that their value cannot leak outside of the current transaction (migration upgrade_to_33.sql)
  • SQL: remove the SET search_path / RESET search_path inside the functions drop_editing_session, editing_survey and split_edge_by_node, which now use the quoted schema name "road_graph". The function merge_editing_session_data has its search_path set in its definition
  • Locator: remove the prefix rr, which was ignored by QGIS (plugin prefixes must have at least 3 characters). The search is run without typing any prefix.

docs.title: Tags, publication, packaging
docs.text:
Tags and version numbers must follow SemVer convention.

To publish a new release, you must:

  • edit the pyproject.toml, change the version number and commit
  • add a new tag (it can be different that the version written in the file.)
  • push to Github (changes and tag)

Every tag pushed to Github will trigger a workflow dispach which will allow to create a Github release with a package for this version:

  • In the project Github repository, go to the tab Actions, menu Release, press the button Run workflows and check the needed options among:
  • Execute dry run
  • Publish to qgis.org then Run workflow

docs.title: Screenshots of the Processing algorithms
docs.text:
The screenshots of the Processing algorithm dialogs, used in the Installation and Import data pages, are generated automatically from the Python algorithms in roadnetwork/processing.

The script .docker/processing_screenshots.py opens each algorithm dialog in QGIS, without any display (Qt offscreen platform), in a temporary QGIS profile with a demo PostgreSQL connection named road_network_demo and the template layers of roadnetwork/resources/import. The images are saved in docs/media/installation and docs/media/user-guide.

To regenerate them locally, with the QGIS docker image (Docker is required):

make processing-screenshots
# Or with another QGIS version
make processing-screenshots QGIS_VERSION=3.40

To add a new algorithm, add its name and the output file name (relative to docs/media) in the ALGORITHMS dictionary of the script, then reference the image in the documentation.

The GitHub workflow .github/workflows/processing-screenshots.yml runs this command whenever the files in roadnetwork/processing are modified on the main branch, and opens a pull request if the screenshots have changed. It can also be run manually from the Actions tab.

docs.title: Presentation of the plugin concepts
docs.text: The RoadNetwork plugin helps to manage a topological county road network and to perform linear referencing with QGIS and PostGIS.

docs.title: Road network
docs.text:
Each road:

  • has an identification, e.g. D907,
  • is composed of a series of ordered edges (simple linestrings).

Markers are positioned along the roads. Their position is often measured with a GPS (X,Y).

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
The road network is a graph built with edges and nodes:

  • each edge has a start node and an end node,
  • an edge can have a previous edge and a next edge,
  • intersecting edges are cut by a node (if they are on the same level).

docs.title: Position and references
docs.text:
This simple organization of roads, edges and markers allows to determine the position of any object based on:

  • a road code: D902,
  • a marker code: 1,
  • an abscissa: 500m.

You can also provide an optional offset, e.g. 3m, and a side, e.g. left.

Any point within a distance of 50m of any road will have its references: D902 PR 1 + 500m (3m left).

docs.title: Linear referencing
docs.text:
Each data object, point or (multi)linestring, is defined by its references calculated from the road network:

  • Points: trees, street lights, car accidents, etc.
  • Linestrings: paintings, safety barriers, roadworks, etc.

We must be able to:

  • calculate the references from the object geometry,
  • create a geometry based on given references:
    • a point,
    • a multi-linestring between two references.

docs.title: Corner cases
docs.text:
Discontinuity: edges could have been deleted (or have changed status).

Roundabouts have their own road code, e.g. GIR D35-D80, and cut the other roads.

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Concept Definition Graph A directed graph made of a set of edges and nodes representing the road network as a road centerline network, matching the axis of the carriageway. Road A consecutive sequence of edges forming a road / a way (e.g. D115). Edge Portion of a road. An edge is a directed segment linking two nodes (simple line). Node The nodes represent the start and end vertices of each edge. Marker Point created by the road network manager, physically materialized on the ground by painted marks associated with kilometer markers. Virtual marker Point created by the GIS administrator to make the administration of the graph easier, especially the computation of the reference point + abscissa. Reference point (PR, point de repère) Formerly known as kilometer point. Business or thematic data Set of thematic data overlaid on the graph and topologically linked to it. It can be point data (e.g. road signs) or linear data (e.g. pavement surface).

docs.title: Useful functions
docs.text:
The road_graph schema provides SQL functions which can be used directly in your queries, for example in the QGIS Browser panel (right-click on the PostgreSQL connection or schema, then Execute SQL…), in psql or in a virtual layer built on a PostgreSQL query.

The examples below use the coordinate reference system EPSG:2154 and the road D613 of the test data of the plugin: the values can be slightly different in your database.

docs.title: Linear referencing functions
docs.text: Function Usage get_reference_from_point References of a point get_road_point_from_reference Point corresponding to references get_road_substring_from_references Line between two references get_spatial_road Geometry of a whole road, with the cumulative distances as measures

docs.title: Get the references of a point
docs.text:
road_graph.get_reference_from_point(_point, _road_code, _use_cache) returns the references of a point, as a JSON object:

SELECT road_graph.get_reference_from_point(
    ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(473136.24, 6895774.58), 2154)
);

{
    "road_code": "D613", "marker_code": 44, "abscissa": 154.50,
    "cumulative": 43063.50, "offset": 15.00, "side": "left"
}
  • _point: the point, in the coordinate reference system of the road graph,
  • _road_code (optional): the code of the road to use. If it is not given, the closest road is used. Give it to choose the road of a point located near an intersection,
  • _use_cache (optional, False by default): used internally to speed up the calculation for many points of the same road.

The function returns NULL if no road is closer than 50 m from the point.

Example: get the references of all the features of a point layer, without storing them:

SELECT
    t.id,
    r.ref->>'road_code' AS road_code,
    (r.ref->>'marker_code')::integer AS marker_code,
    (r.ref->>'abscissa')::real AS abscissa
FROM managed.demo_trees AS t,
LATERAL (SELECT road_graph.get_reference_from_point(t.geom, t.road_code) AS ref) AS r;

docs.title: Get a point from references
docs.text:
road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference(_road_code, _marker_code, _abscissa, _offset, _side) returns the point corresponding to the given references, in the key geom of a JSON object (GeoJSON geometry):

SELECT road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference('D613', 44, 154.5, 15, 'left');

{
    "road_code": "D613", "marker_code": 44, "abscissa": 154.5, "offset": 15, "side": "left",
    "closest_marker_abscissa": 0,
    "geom": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [473136.24, 6895774.58], "crs": {...}}
}
  • _offset: distance in meters from the road axis. Use 0 for a point on the road,
  • _side: left or right, in the direction of the road.

To get a PostGIS geometry:

SELECT ST_GeomFromGeoJSON(
    road_graph.get_road_point_from_reference('D613', 44, 154.5, 15, 'left')->>'geom'
) AS geom;

docs.title: Get a line between two references
docs.text:
road_graph.get_road_substring_from_references(_road_code, _start_marker_code, _start_marker_abscissa, _end_marker_code, _end_marker_abscissa, _offset, _side, _from_first_edge_start, _to_last_edge_end) returns the line of the road between two references, in the key geom of a JSON object:

-- Line of the road D613 between the references 44 + 100 m and 44 + 600 m
SELECT ST_Length(
    (road_graph.get_road_substring_from_references('D613', 44, 100, 44, 600, 0, 'right')->>'geom')::geometry
);
-- 500.00
  • the result is a MultiLineString: the road can be made of several parts, for example on both sides of a roundabout, which has its own road code,
  • _offset and _side: to shift the line from the road axis, e.g. 3 and left for a painting on the left side,
  • _from_first_edge_start and _to_last_edge_end (optional, False by default): extend the line to the start of the edge of the start references, and to the end of the edge of the end references,
  • the start references must be before the end references along the road, else an error is raised. If the start marker is before the first marker of the road, the line starts at the start of the road, and if the end marker is after the last marker, the line ends at the end of the road.

docs.title: Get the geometry of a road with measures
docs.text:
road_graph.get_spatial_road(_road_code) returns the geometry of the whole road, as a MultiLineString with measures (M): the measure of each vertex is its cumulative distance from the start of the road. It can be used with the PostGIS functions of linear referencing, for example ST_LocateAlong:

-- Point located 5000 m after the start of the road D613
SELECT ST_AsText(ST_LocateAlong(road_graph.get_spatial_road('D613'), 5000));
-- MULTIPOINT M ((507254.37 6896996.74 5000))

docs.title: GPS tracks: from a GPX file to the road references
docs.text:
A GPS track recorded on the road, for example with a smartphone and exported as a GPX file, is never exactly on the road graph edges: the GPS precision is usually between 5 and 15 meters.

Two functions allow to transform such a track into road references:

  1. road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track builds a line snapped on the road graph edges from the imprecise GPS track,
  2. road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line returns the ordered list of the roads followed by this line, with the start and end references (marker and abscissa) for each road.

docs.title: Import the GPX file in PostgreSQL
docs.text:
A GPX file can be opened in QGIS with a drag & drop: choose the tracks layer. Then import it in the PostgreSQL database with the QGIS Browser panel: drag & drop the layer from the Layers panel onto the target schema of your PostgreSQL connection. The Processing algorithm Export to PostgreSQL can also be used.

The import can also be done with ogr2ogr:

ogr2ogr -f PostgreSQL PG:"service=my_service" my_track.gpx tracks \
  -nln gps.tracks -lco GEOMETRY_NAME=geom -lco FID=id

Tip

The tracks can stay in the GPS projection EPSG:4326: the functions reproject them automatically to the road graph projection. A geometry without SRID is considered to be already in the road graph projection.

docs.title: Snap the track on the road graph
docs.text:
SELECT road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track(
    _track => t.geom,
    _densify_distance => 2,
    _max_distance => 25,
    _road_change_penalty => 100
) AS geom
FROM gps.tracks AS t
WHERE t.id = 1
;

Only the first parameter is required:

Parameter Default Description _track The GPS track: a linestring or a multilinestring, in any projection _densify_distance 2 Distance in meters between the points added to the track before snapping them _max_distance 25 The track points further than this distance (meters) from any edge are ignored _road_change_penalty 100 Penalty applied each time the road changes. Increase it if the result still has zigzags

The function returns a multilinestring in the road graph projection, which follows exactly the edges geometries, in the direction of the track.

In the example below, the GPS track and its points are displayed in cyan, and the snapped line in green. The track goes from the road D40 to the road D16 through the roundabout GIR_D40_D16-1:

Near the roundabout, the GPS track cuts the curves and crosses the roundabout, whereas the snapped line follows the edges of the 3 roads:

How does it work?

  • The track is densified with a point every _densify_distance meters.
  • For each point, all the roads closer than _max_distance are candidates.
  • Simply taking the closest road for each point would produce zigzags between two close roads (parallel roads, intersections, roundabouts). Instead, the function searches the sequence of roads which minimizes, for the whole track:
    • the distance between the points and their road (multiplied by _densify_distance, which gives approximately the surface in m² between the track and the roads),
    • plus _road_change_penalty each time the road changes between two consecutive points.
  • Each point is then snapped on the closest edge of its road. The small back and forth movements created near the intersections are removed.
  • If two consecutive edges are not connected, for example when a short roundabout section has been skipped, the gap is filled with the shortest path of maximum 5 edges. If no path is found, a new part is created in the multilinestring.
  • The result is built from the edges geometries, from node to node.

docs.title: Get the road sections references
docs.text:
SELECT s.*
FROM road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line(
    road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track(
        ST_GeomFromText('LINESTRING(-0.044052 49.020203, -0.043663 49.019952, ...)', 4326)
    )
) AS s
;

The function returns one line per road section, ordered along the line:

road_order road_code start_marker start_abscissa start_cumulative end_marker end_abscissa end_cumulative direction length 1 D40 14 905.27 16361.8 15 396.15 16761.4 downstream 399.6 2 GIR_D40_D16-1 0 0 0 0 39.17 39.17 downstream 39.17 3 D16 0 716.82 716.82 0 1.62 1.62 upstream 715.19
  • start_marker & start_abscissa: the references of the section start, e.g. 14+905.27,
  • end_marker & end_abscissa: the references of the section end,
  • start_cumulative & end_cumulative: the distances from the road start,
  • direction: downstream if the line follows the road direction, upstream otherwise,
  • length: the section length in meters,
  • geom: the section geometry (linestring).

The second parameter _tolerance (default 1 meter) is the maximum distance between the line and the edges. The line must follow the road graph edges: use the result of get_snapped_line_from_track.

docs.title: Process all the tracks of a table
docs.text:
-- Snapped tracks
CREATE TABLE gps.snapped_tracks AS
SELECT
    t.id,
    road_graph.get_snapped_line_from_track(t.geom) AS geom
FROM gps.tracks AS t
;

-- Road sections of each track
CREATE TABLE gps.track_road_sections AS
SELECT
    st.id AS track_id,
    s.*
FROM gps.snapped_tracks AS st
CROSS JOIN LATERAL road_graph.get_road_sections_from_snapped_line(st.geom) AS s
ORDER BY st.id, s.road_order
;

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• A U-turn in the middle of an edge is not kept: the line leaves the edge by the node it came from.
  • With a very imprecise track (more than ~10 meters) in complex areas like highway interchanges, the result can contain wrong ramps, mainly at the track start or end. Increase _road_change_penalty, or cut the track ends.
  • The points further than _max_distance from the road graph are ignored. If the track leaves the road graph for a long distance, the result can be split into several parts.

docs.title: Database structure
docs.text:
The documentation of the road_graph schema (tables, views, columns, constraints, relationships and functions) is generated by SchemaSpy.
