docs.title: Tables and fields
docs.text:
The plugin stores the road graph in the PostgreSQL schema road_graph. The schema road_graph_editing has the same tables: it is the sandbox of the editing sessions.

This page describes the fields of the main tables. For the technical details (types, constraints, indexes, functions, etc.), see the Database structure.

The created_at and updated_at fields of the tables are filled automatically, and the uid fields contain a unique identifier (UUID) generated automatically.

docs.title: roads
docs.text:
The list of the roads. This table has no geometry: the geometry of a road is made of its edges.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) road_code text Code of the road, e.g. D613. Unique. Used by the edges and the markers to refer to the road. road_type text road or roundabout. The roundabouts are managed differently by the trigger functions (see Create a roundabout). road_class text Class of the road: Départementale, Nationale, Autoroute, etc. It must exist in the table glossary_road_class. road_class_code text Code of the road class, e.g. the code of the French department is_active boolean If the road is active road_topic text Optional topic of the road, e.g. Port is_access_road boolean If the road is an access road

docs.title: edges
docs.text:
The edges of the road graph: each edge is a portion of a road between two nodes, drawn in the direction of the road.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) road_code text Code of the road of the edge geom LineString Geometry of the edge. Its coordinates are rounded to 10 cm, except for the roundabouts. start_node integer Identifier of the start node (upstream node), filled automatically end_node integer Identifier of the end node (downstream node), filled automatically previous_edge_id integer Identifier of the previous edge of the same road, filled automatically if an edge of the same road ends at the start node. Empty for the first edge of the road. next_edge_id integer Identifier of the next edge of the same road. Empty for the last edge of the road. start_marker integer Code of the marker before the start point of the edge start_abscissa real Distance in meters between this marker and the start point start_cumulative real Cumulative distance in meters from the start of the road to the start point end_marker integer Code of the marker before the end point of the edge end_abscissa real Distance in meters between this marker and the end point end_cumulative real Cumulative distance in meters from the start of the road to the end point no_intersection_cutting boolean If True, the edge is not cut automatically at its intersections with the other edges, for example a bridge (see Edges which must not be cut). Default: False. id_source text Identifier of the edge in the source data, after an import

The references of the edges (start_marker, start_abscissa, start_cumulative, end_marker, end_abscissa and end_cumulative) are calculated automatically by the trigger functions each time an edge or a marker of the road is modified.

docs.title: nodes
docs.text:
The nodes of the road graph: the start and end points of the edges, and the intersections between the edges.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) geom Point Geometry of the node. Two nodes cannot have the same geometry.

The nodes are created and deleted automatically by the trigger functions when the edges are edited. Creating or moving a node on an edge splits this edge.

docs.title: markers
docs.text:
The markers (reference points, PR in French) positioned along the roads.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) road_code text Code of the road of the marker code integer Code of the marker, e.g. 12 for PR 12. Positive. abscissa real Abscissa of the marker in meters. 0 for a real marker, and the distance from the marker of the same code for a virtual marker, e.g. 613 for PR 72 + 613m. Positive. is_virtual boolean True for a virtual marker (PRV), created to make the administration of the graph easier geom Point Geometry of the marker id_source text Identifier of the marker in the source data, after an import

A road cannot have two markers with the same code and abscissa. A marker 0 is created automatically at the start of a new road, except for the roundabouts.

docs.title: glossary_road_class
docs.text:
The list of the road classes used by the field road_class of the table roads.

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) code text Code of the class, e.g. Départementale. Unique. label text Label of the class. Unique.

docs.title: editing_sessions
docs.text:
The editing sessions: the areas in which the road graph is edited in the sandbox (see Road graph editing).

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) label text Short label of the session author text Author of the session description text Description of the session geom Polygon Area of the session. It cannot be modified once the data has been cloned. status text Status of the session: created, cloned, edited unique_code text Code generated automatically with the creation date, e.g. editing_session_2026_10_28_08_37_24 cloned_ids jsonb Identifiers of the objects copied into the sandbox (roads, edges, nodes, markers) logged_ids jsonb Identifiers of the objects created, updated or deleted in the sandbox, used to merge the session

docs.title: managed_objects
docs.text:
The list of the business tables based on the road graph (see Managed objects).

Field Type Description id integer Unique identifier (automatic) schema_name text Schema of the business table table_name text Name of the business table. A table can be registered only once. geometry_type text Geometry type of the table: POINT, LINESTRING or MULTILINESTRING update_policy_on_graph_change text Update rule when the road graph changes: references (the geometry is kept and the references are updated) or geometry (the references are kept and the geometry is updated) add_trigger_on_geom_change boolean If True, the function road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers() creates on the table the trigger calculating the references automatically. Default: False. last_update timestamp Date of the last update of the objects of the table last_updated_objects_ids integer[] Identifiers of the objects updated by the last update

docs.title: metadata
docs.text:
The version of the database structure, used by the plugin to know which upgrades must be run.

Field Type Description me_version text Version of the database structure me_version_date date Date of the version me_status integer Status of the version

docs.title: Views
docs.text: View Description v_road_without_zero_marker The roads which do not have a marker 0 v_managed_objects The objects of the business tables updated by the last merge of an editing session, as a 10 m buffer vm_managed_objects Materialized view of v_managed_objects, refreshed at the end of each merge (see Last updated objects)

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
To use the plugin, you need to:

  • install QGIS Desktop
  • install the plugin for QGIS
  • add a connection to a PostgreSQL database with PostGIS extension
  • install the database structure on this PostgreSQL database

docs.title: Get QGIS Desktop
docs.text:
The administrator must use the QGIS desktop software, version 3.40.x or above, to edit these needed metadata.

You can download QGIS in the official download page

docs.title: Install the plugin
docs.text:
At present, the plugin is not yet in QGIS official plugin repository. To install the plugin, you need to:

  • open QGIS Plugin manager (menu Plugins)
  • In the All tab, search for the word RoadNetwork and install the RoadNetwork plugin.

After a successful installation, you should see a new dock called RoadNetwork

For further details, you can have a look at 3liz documentation web page.

docs.title: Add a connection to the PostgreSQL database
docs.text:
The plugin stores all the data in a PostgreSQL database, with the PostGIS extension installed (to manage spatial data).

You need to have access to a PostgreSQL database, with enough rights to create a database schema and tables inside this schema.

In QGIS, use the Datasource manager under the Layer menu to create a new PostgreSQL connection:

  • Activate the PostgreSQL tab (elephant icon)
  • Click on the New button
  • In the creation dialog, fill the needed information, and use the Test connection button to make sure the credentials are ok.

We advise to:

  • use a service connection instead of the basic authentication. See QGIS documentation
  • check the boxes Use estimated table metadata and Also list tables with no geometry

Once your connection is set up, you can create the database structure in your PostgreSQL database

docs.title: Configure the plugin
docs.text:
This algorithm will allow to configure the extension for the current QGIS project.

You must run this script before any other script.

Parameters:

  • PostgreSQL connection to the database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the current QGIS project. This connection will be used for the other algorithms.

docs.title: Create the database structure
docs.text:
Install the database structure with tables and function on the chosen database connection.

This script will add a road_graph schema with needed tables and functions.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the installation.
  • Overwrite the database schema and all data ?: if the schema already exists in the database, the algorithm stops with an error, unless this box is checked. In this case, the existing schema is dropped with all its data and created again. Unchecked by default.
  • Geometry CRS: coordinate reference system of the geometries stored in the database. It must be a valid EPSG code. Default: EPSG:2154 - RGF93 v1 / Lambert-93.

docs.title: Upgrade database structure
docs.text:
Upgrade the tables and functions in the chosen database.

If you have upgraded your QGIS plugin, you can run this script to upgrade your database to the new plugin version.

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the upgrade.
  • Check this box to upgrade. No action will be done otherwise: safety checkbox. The algorithm refuses to run if it is not checked.

The coordinate reference system is not asked: it is read from the existing edges table.

docs.title: Create your database local interface
docs.text:
This algorithm will create a new QGIS project file for administration purpose.

The generated QGIS project must then be opened by the administrator to edit the road network data by using QGIS editing capabilities

Parameters:

  • Connection to the PostgreSQL database: name of the database connection you would like to use for the new QGIS project.
  • Geometry CRS: coordinate reference system of the QGIS project and its layers. Use the same CRS as the one chosen when creating the database structure. Default: EPSG:2154 - RGF93 v1 / Lambert-93.
  • QGIS project file to create: choose the output file destination. We advise you to choose a name reflecting the database name.

You can then open the generated QGIS project.

docs.title: Lizmap Web Client tools
docs.text:
The road network can be published with Lizmap Web Client (LWC). A JavaScript script, road_network.js, adds tools to the web map so that users can work with linear references (road, marker, abscissa, offset and side) directly in the browser.

These tools rely on Lizmap actions: each tool calls a named action, which runs the PostgreSQL function lizmap_get_data(json). This function calls the road_graph functions of the plugin and returns the result as GeoJSON.

Note

The user interface is written in English and can be translated. This page gives the labels of the French interface, with the English text.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The script adds four tools:

Tool Where Lizmap actions used Road network panel Mini-dock Graphe routier get_references_from_point, get_road_point_from_reference Create a geometry from references Editing form get_references_from_point, get_road_point_from_reference, get_road_substring_from_references, get_edge_start_or_end_tip_from_references Split a line Feature popup split_line_by_point Merge two lines Feature popup merge_selected_lines

docs.title: Road network panel
docs.text:
The script adds a mini-dock named Graphe routier (Road network). It opens when the map loads.

The panel contains a form with these fields:

Label Meaning Route Road code, for example D1. The list of values comes from the roads layer. PR Marker code (in French: point de repère) Abscisse Abscissa: distance in meters from the marker Cumul Cumulative distance in meters from the start of the road (read-only) Décalage Offset: distance in meters from the road axis Côté Side of the road: Gauche (left) or Droite (right)

docs.title: Get the references of a point
docs.text: When the panel is open, click on the map. The script runs the action get_references_from_point with the clicked point. The returned references fill the form, and the point is displayed on the map.

docs.title: Show the references when hovering the map
docs.text:
Check Activer le calcul au survol (Enable calculation on hover). When the mouse moves over the map, a tooltip displays the references of the point under the cursor, for example D1 - PR 3 + 250m (2m G). The values in the form are updated too.

To limit the number of requests to the server:

  • the script sends at most one request every 200 ms,
  • no request is sent while the user drags the map.

This option is not available while the editing form is open.

docs.title: Center the map on references
docs.text:
Type a road, a marker, an abscissa, an offset and a side in the form, then click Centrer (Center). The script runs the action get_road_point_from_reference and centers the map on the returned point.

Tip

Click and hover only work at scale 1:50,000 or larger. At a smaller scale, a message asks the user to zoom in.

docs.title: Create a geometry from references
docs.text:
When the user opens the Lizmap editing form for a point or line layer, the script adds a collapsible section above the form: Create the geometry from references.

The fields depend on the geometry type of the layer:

  • Point layer: road, marker, abscissa, offset and side.
  • Line layer: road, start marker and abscissa (PR début, Abscisse début), end marker and abscissa (PR fin, Abscisse fin), offset and side.

If the editing form has a field named road_code, its value is copied into the Route field.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
Button Action Create Computes the geometry from the references and replaces the geometry of the edited feature. For a point layer, the script runs get_road_point_from_reference. For a line layer, it runs get_road_substring_from_references. If the start references are after the end references, the script swaps them. Reset Deletes the drawn geometry and resets the reference fields. Edge, start row Sets the start references to the start of the edge located at the start references. Road, start row Sets the start references to the start of the road. Edge, end row Sets the end references to the end of the edge located at the end references. Road, end row Sets the end references to the end of the road.

The Tronçon and Route buttons are only available for line layers. They run the action get_edge_start_or_end_tip_from_references. After that, the line geometry is computed again.

docs.title: Snap a drawn geometry to the road
docs.text:
When the user draws or modifies the geometry with the Lizmap drawing tools, the script:

  1. runs get_references_from_point for the point, or for the first and last vertices of the line,
  2. fills the reference fields with the returned values,
  3. replaces the drawn geometry with the geometry computed from these references.

As a result, the geometry always follows the road. If the road field has a value, only this road is used to find the references.

If no reference is found after 2 seconds, a message tells the user that the geometry could not be created. The most common cause is a point more than 50 m away from the road.

When the feature is saved, the Graphe routier panel opens again.

docs.title: Split a line at a point
docs.text:
This tool adds a button to the popup of the features of a line layer. It splits a line in two features at a point.

The button is only displayed if the user can modify the geometry and create features in this layer, in the Lizmap editing configuration.

  1. Open the Graphe routier panel and click on the line where it must be split. A red point is displayed on the map.
  2. In the popup of the line, click the button. Its label is the title of the split_line_by_point action.
  3. Confirm the operation.

The script sends the red point to the action split_line_by_point. The database function road_graph.split_table_linestring_feature_by_point splits the line, and the layer is refreshed.

The default popup button of this action is hidden, because it does not send the clicked point.

docs.title: Merge two lines
docs.text:
This tool adds a button to the popup of the features of a line layer. It merges two features of the same layer into one feature.

The button is only displayed if the user can modify the geometry and delete features in this layer, in the Lizmap editing configuration.

  1. In the popup of the first line, click Choose this feature to merge. The button label becomes Feature chosen to merge. To cancel, click this button again.
  2. Click on the second line on the map. In its popup, click Merge with the chosen feature.
  3. Confirm the operation.

The script runs the action merge_selected_lines with the IDs of the two features. The database function road_graph.merge_table_linestring_features merges them and the layer is refreshed. The popup then shows only the merged feature.

Once a first feature is chosen, the merge button is only displayed for features of the same layer.

docs.title: 1. Publish the layers
docs.text:
In the QGIS project:

  • add the road_graph.edges layer. The actions about references use this layer.
  • add the road_graph.roads layer and publish it as WFS (Project properties > QGIS Server > WFS capabilities). The script uses it to fill the list of roads. The layer must have the fields id, road_code and road_order.
  • for the split and merge tools, add the line layers that the users can edit.

docs.title: 2. Create the database function
docs.text:
Create the function public.lizmap_get_data(json) in the database. The file lizmap_get_data_example.sql gives a complete example for all the actions.

The function uses the projection EPSG:2154. Change it if your data uses another projection.

docs.title: 3. Create the actions file
docs.text:
Create a file named after the QGIS project, with the extension .action. For example, for road_network.qgs, create road_network.qgs.action in the same folder.

The file lizmap_action_file_example.json gives a complete example. Update it:

  • replace edges_7df8a321_25e8_4a67_9bf8_796e4782e147 with the ID of your edges layer,
  • replace demo_painting_26eb3c57_3374_41a5_8628_391caa42f33a with the IDs of the line layers for the split and merge tools. Do this in layers and in callbacks.

The action names must not change, because the script uses them.

Action Scope Options Returned feature get_references_from_point layer road_code, vertex_number Point with road_code, marker_code, abscissa, cumulative, offset, side, vertex_number get_road_point_from_reference layer road_code, marker_code, abscissa, offset, side Point with the references get_road_substring_from_references layer road_code, start_marker_code, start_abscissa, end_marker_code, end_abscissa, offset, side Multilinestring with the start and end references get_edge_start_or_end_tip_from_references layer road_code, marker_code, abscissa, start_or_end (start or end), tip_type (edge or road) Point with marker_code, abscissa, start_or_end split_line_by_point feature none (the clicked point is sent as WKT) The clicked point, message and message_detail merge_selected_lines layer feature_id_a, feature_id_b message and message_detail, no geometry

vertex_number tells the script where to put the result: -1 for the panel, 0 for the start point and 1 for the end point of the edited geometry.

docs.title: 4. Configure the script
docs.text:
Open road_network.js and edit the CONFIGURATION section at the top of the file:

Constant Default value Description ROAD_MIN_SCALE 50000 Smallest scale denominator for the click and hover tools ROAD_ROADS_LAYER_NAME roads WFS name of the roads layer ROAD_EDGES_LAYER_ID edges_7df8a321_... QGIS ID of the edges layer ROAD_ORDER_FIELD road_order Field used to sort the list of roads

Do not edit the code below the END CONFIGURATION comment.

docs.title: 5. Add the files to Lizmap
docs.text:
Follow the Lizmap documentation: Adding your own JavaScript.

  1. Allow JavaScript for the repository in the Lizmap administration (Allow themes/JavaScript codes for this repository).
  2. Copy road_network.js, road_network.css and road_network.csv into the repository folder:
    • media/js/<project_name>/ to use the tools in one project,
    • media/js/default/ to use them in all projects of the repository.
  3. Reload the map in the browser.

docs.title: Translate the interface
docs.text:
The texts of the interface are written in English in the script. The translations are stored in a CSV file located next to the script. This file has the same name as the script, with the .csv extension: road_network.csv for road_network.js.

When the map loads, the script:

  1. gets the language of the user interface, from the lang attribute of the page or from the browser language,
  2. downloads the CSV file,
  3. displays the translated texts. A text without a translation is displayed in English.

If the CSV file is not found, the interface is displayed in English.

The first line of the file contains the language codes. The first column contains the English text, exactly as written in the script. Each other column contains the translations for one language:

en,fr
Road network,Graphe routier
Road,Route
"Please zoom in to at least 1:{scale} to display the references","Veuillez zoomer au moins au 1/{scale} pour afficher les références"

To add a language, add a column with its two-letter code, for example de or es.

Rules for the values:

  • enclose a value in double quotes if it contains a comma, a double quote or a new line,
  • double the double quotes inside a value: "",
  • keep the placeholders in braces, for example {scale}, and do not translate them. They are replaced by values when the text is displayed. They can be moved in the sentence.

docs.title: Texts of the actions and of the database
docs.text:
The same CSV file also translates:

  • the title and confirm properties of the actions, in the .qgs.action file. Write them in English, and add them to the CSV file.
  • the messages returned by the lizmap_get_data function, in the message field. Lizmap displays them at the top of the map, and the script replaces them by their translation.

A message can contain a variable part, for example the detail of an error returned by the database. In this case, the lizmap_get_data function must also return this variable part in a message_detail field, and the message must end with it:

Field Value message An error occurred while splitting the line: The point is not close enough to the feature (distance 12 > 5m) message_detail The point is not close enough to the feature (distance 12 > 5m)

In the CSV file, the variable part is replaced by the {detail} placeholder:

"An error occurred while splitting the line: {detail}","Une erreur s'est produite lors de la découpe de la ligne : {detail}"

The variable part itself is not translated.

If you change a text in the .qgs.action file or in the lizmap_get_data function, change it in the CSV file too. Otherwise, the text is displayed without translation.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• The script was written for a specific version of Lizmap Web Client. It may not work with another version.
  • The tools only support point and line layers.
  • The start and end references of a line must be on the same road.
  • The split and merge tools are not available for the edges layer.

docs.title: User guide
docs.text:
The RoadNetwork plugin stores all the business logic inside a PostgreSQL database. The QGIS plugin helps to create and upgrade this database, to visualize the road network, to edit it safely and to keep the business data up to date.

This guide is split in five parts:

  • Import data: how to import the road graph (edges and markers) into the database, and how to create a demo database.
  • QGIS project and tools: the administration project, the toolbar and panels of the plugin, and the tools available to search and get references.
  • Processing algorithms: the algorithms provided by the plugin.
  • Road graph editing: how to edit the roads, edges and markers in a dedicated editing session.
  • Managed objects: how to prepare the business data based on the road network, and how they are kept up to date when the graph changes.

docs.title: Database model
docs.text:
All the logic is stored inside a PostgreSQL database:

  • a simple set of tables: roads, edges, nodes, markers, glossary_road_class, managed_objects, and some views,
  • many functions to calculate references and geometries, among them:
    • get_road_point_from_reference
    • get_road_substring_from_references
    • update_table_references_from_geometries
    • update_table_geometry_from_references
  • trigger functions in charge of maintaining the road network topology: automatic node creation, split of intersected edges, etc.

See Tables and fields for the description of the fields of the tables, and the Database structure documentation for a complete description of the tables and functions.

docs.title: Administration tools
docs.text:
The plugin provides QGIS Processing algorithms which allow to:

  • create the database structure with all the tables, functions, etc.: Create database structure,
  • upgrade the structure automatically when upgrading the plugin: Upgrade database structure,
  • create a QGIS administration project with all the layers, styles, labels, actions, etc.: Create database local interface,
  • import data from template edges and markers tables: Import data from template.

These algorithms, described in Processing algorithms, are available in the QGIS Processing toolbox and in the RoadNetwork administration panel, which also shows the database connection used by the project and checks that the plugin and database versions match.

docs.title: Editing rules
docs.text:
The road graph data are not edited directly in the production schema road_graph, but in a dedicated editing session schema road_graph_editing, which acts as a sandbox:

  1. The user draws a polygon in the editing_sessions layer around the area to edit. The new editing session has the status created.
  2. The algorithm Clone data to a new editing session (toolbar button Clone data to the editing sandbox, or layer action Create editing session) copies an extract of the production data inside this polygon into the sandbox. The status becomes cloned.

3. The editing is made with the QGIS tools: forms, topological editing, etc. The status becomes edited after the first change. * QGIS automatic transaction grouping is activated in the project: the changes made by the database triggers (node creation, edge split, etc.) are visible live. * A layer action helps to create roundabouts, see Create a roundabout.

4. The algorithm Merge editing session data (toolbar button Merge editing sandbox data) merges the modifications back into the road_graph schema and updates the managed objects. The sandbox data and the merged editing session are then deleted.

At any time, the modifications of the editing session can be highlighted with the action Display edited data, and the editing session can be cancelled with the action Drop editing session.

docs.title: Editing session actions
docs.text: The editing_sessions layer has three layer actions. To run an action on an editing session, use the Identify Features tool and right-click on the editing session polygon in the map, or use the Run Feature Action tool of the Attributes toolbar. See also Layer actions.

docs.title: Create editing session
docs.text: This action opens the algorithm Clone data to a new editing session, which copies the production data inside the last created editing session polygon into the editing schema, like the toolbar button Clone data to the editing sandbox. It is a layer action: it is available in the Actions menu of the editing_sessions attribute table toolbar, and does not need any selected feature.

docs.title: Display edited data
docs.text:
This action highlights in the map the objects modified in the editing session, from the content of its logged_ids column of the layer editing_sessions. The objects flash with a color depending on the modification:

Color Modification Layer used to display the object Yellow Updated the editing layer, e.g. edges copie Red Deleted the production layer, e.g. edges Green Inserted the editing layer, e.g. edges copie

The edges, nodes and markers are displayed. A message is displayed if the editing session does not contain any modification.

docs.title: Drop editing session
docs.text:
This action deletes the editing session and all the data of the editing schema road_graph_editing, with the database function road_graph.drop_editing_session. The modifications which have not been merged are lost: a confirmation is asked before.

The action is cancelled with a warning if:

  • the editing_sessions layer is not in editing mode,
  • the tool Get references on hover is activated: uncheck the checkbox Get references on hover ? in the Road network tools panel before.

You may have to refresh the map canvas to see the changes.

Info

Do not forget to save the state by clicking on the Save button of QGIS editing toolbar.

docs.title: Create a roundabout
docs.text:
Roundabouts have their own road code, e.g. GIR_D40_D80, and cut the other roads (see Concepts). The road of the roundabout must exist in the roads layer with the road type roundabout.

To create a roundabout in the editing session:

  1. Toggle editing on the edges layer.
  2. Use the QGIS shape digitizing tool Circle by a center point and another point to draw the roundabout circle, and give it the road code of the roundabout.
  3. Once the circle is created, the database trigger functions automatically split the circle into edges at each intersection with the edges of the existing crossroads.
  4. Right-click on one of the edges of the roundabout circle with the Identify Features tool, and choose the action Finalize the roundabout.

This layer action of the edges copie layer runs the database function clean_digitized_roundabout, which:

  • deletes the pieces of edges inside the roundabout, and updates the previous and next edges of the remaining roads,
  • deletes the node created by QGIS at the top of the circle, by merging the two edges around it,
  • adds a marker 0 for this roundabout, on its westernmost node, if it does not already exist.

The action is cancelled with a warning if the layer is not in editing mode, or if the road type of the selected edge is not roundabout. You may have to refresh the map canvas to see the changes.

docs.title: Edges which must not be cut
docs.text:
By default, the database trigger functions keep the graph topology up to date while you edit:

  • when an edge is drawn or its geometry is modified, a node is created at each intersection of this edge with the other edges, and the crossing edges are split by this node. If a node already exists less than 50 cm from the intersection, it is used instead.
  • when a node is created or moved on an edge, far enough from its start and end points, this edge is split by the node. This is also the case of the start or end node of an edge being drawn, for example a new road arriving in the middle of another road.

Only the intersections of the drawn or modified edge are processed, and only inside the editing session polygon. The intersections between the other edges are kept as they are: two edges crossing each other without a node, for example at an existing bridge, stay without a node, even when one of them is split by the drawn edge.

But two roads drawn on top of each other are not always connected: a highway crossing a road on a bridge, a road going through a tunnel, the access roads of a highway interchange, etc. For these edges, check the field No intersection cutting (no_intersection_cutting) in the edge form. It can be changed at any time, for example before drawing or modifying a road which crosses a bridge.

An edge with no_intersection_cutting set to True:

  • is not split at its intersections with the other edges, and does not split them: no node is created at these intersections, whether the field is set on the drawn edge or on the crossed edge,
  • is not split by the existing nodes located under it, for example a crossroad of the roads located under a bridge, even when such a node is moved,
  • is split when the start or end point of a drawn or moved edge is located on it, far enough from its own start and end points: for example a new access road arriving in the middle of a highway edge. This makes sense since the two roads are really connected at this point.

The value of the field is kept when an edge is split: the new parts have the same value.

The diagram below shows when an edge is split:

graph TD A[A node is created or moved on an edge,<br>or a drawn or modified edge crosses it] --> B{Field No intersection cutting<br>of this edge, or of the drawn edge} B -->|False| C[The edge is split] B -->|True| D{Is the node the start or end point<br>of the edge being drawn or moved?} D -->|Yes, e.g. a new access road<br>arriving on a highway| C D -->|No, e.g. a road crossing<br>under a bridge| E[The edge is not split]

Tip

Before drawing a new road which crosses a highway interchange without being connected to it, set the field to True for the new edge, or for the crossed highway and access roads edges: no node will be created at these intersections, and only the roads really connected will be split.

docs.title: How to edit the data in QGIS
docs.text:
In QGIS, you can edit the layer data by toggling the editing mode for each layer:

  • Select the layer in the panel by clicking on it: the layer is highlighted in blue
  • Right-click on the layer name and select Toggle Editing or use the menu Layer / Toggle Editing

To add a new record, select the layer in the Layers panel, then use the menu Edit / Add Record (or CTRL+.). It will open a form which lets you enter the needed data. Once every required fields have been filled, validate with the OK button on the bottom-right.

To view all the records of a layer, select the layer in the Layers panel, then open the attribute table with the menu Layer / Open Attribute Table (or F6)

You can undo previous modifications with the menu Edit / Undo (or CTRL+Z).

To permanently save the changed data in the layer, you need to use the menu Layer / Save Layer Edits. After saving the data, you will not be able to undo your changes (but you can always reopen the data and changed the values).

To edit a record, open the layer attribute table, and then click on the small button Switch to form view on the bottom-right of the dialog (the first one). Then select a record in the left panel, and use the displayed form to edit the data.

To delete a record, select the record in the attribute table by clicking on the line number on the left: the line must be highlighted in blue. Then use the trash icon Delete selected features (or Del). You can undo the deletion if you have not yet saved layer edits.

docs.title: Import the road graph: edges and markers
docs.text:
The road graph tables roads, edges, nodes and markers can be filled from two vector layers: one for the edges and one for the markers.

These layers must follow the structure of the template files provided with the plugin, in the folder roadnetwork/resources/import/ of the plugin:

  • source_edges.fgb for the edges,
  • source_markers.fgb for the markers.

You can open these FlatGeobuf files in QGIS to see example data.

docs.title: Edges layer
docs.text:
Each feature is an edge, i.e. a portion of a road between two nodes, drawn in the direction of the road.

  • Geometry: LineString, or MultiLineString with only one part (only the first part of a multi-part geometry is imported).
  • Columns:
Column Type Description road_code text Code of the road, e.g. D248. The roads are created from the distinct values. edge_order integer Order of the edge in its road, from the start of the road: 1, 2, 3, etc. road_type text road or roundabout road_class text Class of the road. It must exist in the table glossary_road_class, e.g. Départementale road_class_code text Code of the road class, e.g. the code of the French department is_active boolean If the road is active road_topic text Optional topic of the road, e.g. Port. Can be empty. is_access_road boolean If the road is an access road id_source text Identifier of the feature in the source data. Can be empty.

The previous and next edges of each edge are calculated from the edge_order column.

docs.title: Markers layer
docs.text:
Each feature is a marker (reference point, PR) positioned along a road.

  • Geometry: Point, or MultiPoint with only one point.
  • Columns:
Column Type Description road_code text Code of the road of the marker. It must correspond to a road_code of the edges layer. code integer Code of the marker, e.g. 12 for PR 12. Must be positive. abscissa real Abscissa of the marker, in meters. Must be positive. Use 0 for the real markers. is_virtual boolean True for a virtual marker, False for a real marker. id_source text Identifier of the feature in the source data. Can be empty.

A marker 0 with an abscissa 0 is automatically created at the start of each road, if it does not already exist.

docs.title: Run the import
docs.text:
Use the Processing algorithm Import data from template, also available with the button Import data of the RoadNetwork administration panel:

  • PostgreSQL connection to the database: the database where the plugin structure has been installed,
  • Edges: the edges layer,
  • Markers: the markers layer.

The algorithm:

  1. checks that the layers contain the required columns,
  2. copies the layers in temporary tables, reprojected to the coordinate reference system of the database,
  3. runs the database function road_graph.import_data_from_template_tables, which:
    • checks the values of road_type and road_class,
    • creates the roads, the nodes at the start and end of each edge, the edges and the markers,
    • calculates the references of the edges (start and end markers, abscissas and cumulative distances),
  4. displays the number of imported roads, edges, nodes and markers, and drops the temporary tables.

Note

This import is designed to initialize an empty road graph. Existing objects are not updated: conflicting data are ignored.

docs.title: Create a demo database
docs.text:
The template files provided with the plugin contain a complete demo road graph, in Normandy (France), in the coordinate reference system EPSG:2154 - RGF93 v1 / Lambert-93:

  • 2,260 roads: departmental and national roads, highways, roundabouts, etc.,
  • 7,809 edges,
  • 13,774 markers.

It is useful to train the users or to test the features of the plugin without modifying the production data.

Since the plugin schema is always road_graph, a database contains only one road graph: use a dedicated PostgreSQL database for the demo, for example road_network_demo, with the PostGIS extension.

  1. In QGIS, add a connection to this database, and configure the plugin with it.
  2. Run the algorithm Create database structure, with the default coordinate reference system EPSG:2154.
  3. Open the template files source_edges.fgb and source_markers.fgb in QGIS. They are stored in the plugin folder: use the menu Settings / User Profiles / Open Active Profile Folder, then open the folder python/plugins/roadnetwork/resources/import/.
  4. Run the algorithm Import data from template with these two layers, as described above.
  5. Run the algorithm Create database local interface to create the QGIS administration project of the demo database, and open it.

To add some demo business data, follow the examples of the page Managed objects.

docs.title: Business data
docs.text: To import your business data (road signs, safety barriers, etc.) and calculate their references, see Managed objects: add a business table.

docs.title: Managed objects
docs.text:
The local authorities manage a lot of data based on the road network: roadworks, asphalt rehabilitation, road signs, hedge pruning, etc.

Each data object, point or (multi)linestring, is defined by its references calculated from the road network (see Concepts). They are stored in your own PostgreSQL tables, called managed objects. When the road graph is modified, these objects must be updated.

docs.title: The managed objects layer
docs.text:
The managed_objects layer lists all the PostgreSQL tables impacted by any graph modification, with the update policy to apply to each of them:

id schema_name table_name geometry_type update_policy_on_graph_change add_trigger_on_geom_change 1 managed demo_trees POINT references True 2 managed demo_safety_barriers MULTILINESTRING geometry False
  • schema_name and table_name: the business table,
  • geometry_type: the geometry type of the table, e.g. POINT or MULTILINESTRING,
  • update_policy_on_graph_change: the rule chosen by the administrator:
    • references: the geometry is kept and the references are updated,
    • geometry: the references are kept and the geometry is updated.
  • add_trigger_on_geom_change: if True, the trigger calculating the references is created on this table by the function road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers() (see below). Default: False.

Each table must have the reference columns corresponding to its geometry type. They can be added automatically with the function road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields, for one table or for all the tables of this layer (see Add the reference fields).

docs.title: Add a business table
docs.text:
To manage a new business table with the road graph:

  1. prepare the table, with its reference columns,
  2. register it in the managed_objects layer,
  3. add the reference columns if needed,
  4. calculate the references of its features,
  5. optionally, calculate automatically the references of the features created or moved afterwards.

docs.title: Prepare the table
docs.text:
The table must have:

  • a primary key,
  • a geometry column geom, in the same coordinate reference system as the road graph, of type Point for point objects, or LineString / MultiLineString for linear objects,
  • a text column road_code,
  • the reference columns, which are calculated from the road graph:
Geometry type Required columns Optional columns Point marker_code (integer), abscissa (real) cumulative (real), offset (real), side (text) (Multi)LineString start_marker_code (integer), start_abscissa (real), end_marker_code (integer), end_abscissa (real) start_cumulative, end_cumulative (real), offset (real), side (text)

For example, for a table of trees:

CREATE TABLE managed.demo_trees (
    id integer PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    species text NOT NULL,
    road_code text,
    marker_code integer,
    abscissa real,
    side text,
    "offset" real,
    cumulative real,
    geom geometry(POINT, 2154)
);

The reference columns can also be added automatically, once the table is created, with the function road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields (see Add the reference fields).

Then import your data into this table, for example with the QGIS tools (drag and drop in the Browser panel, or the Processing algorithm Export to PostgreSQL), or with SQL.

docs.title: Register the table
docs.text:
Add the table in the managed_objects layer (table road_graph.managed_objects), with its schema name, table name, geometry type and update policy:

INSERT INTO road_graph.managed_objects (
    schema_name, table_name, geometry_type, update_policy_on_graph_change
)
VALUES ('managed', 'demo_trees', 'POINT', 'references');

docs.title: Add the reference fields
docs.text:
The function road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields adds to a table the reference columns listed above, depending on its geometry type. The geometry type is read from the managed_objects layer if the table is registered, or else from its geometry column geom.

For example, for a table of road signs which does not have the reference columns yet:

CREATE TABLE managed.road_signs (
    id integer PRIMARY KEY GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY,
    label text,
    geom geometry(POINT, 2154)
);

-- Add the reference fields
SELECT * FROM road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields('managed', 'road_signs');

The function returns one line per column, with its status:

field_name field_type field_status road_code text added marker_code integer added abscissa real added cumulative real added offset real added side text added
  • The existing columns are not modified: their status is already exists, or already exists with the type ... if their type is not the expected one. The function can therefore be run several times.
  • The optional columns (cumulative, start_cumulative, end_cumulative, offset and side) are not added if the third parameter is False: road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields('managed', 'road_signs', False).
  • If the columns cannot be added, the function returns one line with the status table not found, geom column not found or geometry type not supported: ....

To add the reference columns to all the tables listed in the managed_objects layer:

SELECT o.schema_name, o.table_name, f.field_name, f.field_type, f.field_status
FROM road_graph.managed_objects AS o
CROSS JOIN LATERAL road_graph.add_managed_object_reference_fields(o.schema_name, o.table_name) AS f
ORDER BY o.id;

Tip

The column road_code is added empty. If it is still empty when the references are calculated, the references are calculated on the closest road, and the column road_code is filled. Fill it beforehand to force the road of a feature, for example at an intersection.

docs.title: Calculate the references
docs.text:
Once the features have been imported, calculate their references from their geometries with the database function road_graph.update_table_references_from_geometries:

-- Calculate the references of all the features of the table
SELECT road_graph.update_table_references_from_geometries('managed', 'demo_trees', NULL);

-- Calculate the references of the features of some roads only
SELECT road_graph.update_table_references_from_geometries('managed', 'demo_trees', ARRAY['D138', 'D152']);

The function parameters are the schema name, the table name, and an optional list of road codes. For each feature:

  • if the column road_code is filled, the references are calculated on this road,
  • if it is empty, the closest road is used, and the column road_code is filled.

It returns the number of updated features and their ids, for example:

{"nb": 7, "last_updated_objects_ids": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]}

If your data contain the references but no geometry, use instead the function road_graph.update_table_geometries_from_references, with the same parameters, to calculate the geometries from the references.

docs.title: Automatic calculation of the references
docs.text:
The trigger function road_graph.calculate_managed_object_references calculates the references of a managed object feature each time it is inserted or its geometry is updated. The table must be listed in road_graph.managed_objects, and have a road_code and a geom column.

The function road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers() creates this trigger, named trg_calculate_managed_object_references, on every table listed in road_graph.managed_objects with the column add_trigger_on_geom_change set to True. Run it after adding new tables in the managed objects layer, or after checking this column:

SELECT * FROM road_graph.add_managed_objects_triggers();

It can be run several times: the trigger is only created when it does not already exist. Unchecking add_trigger_on_geom_change does not remove an existing trigger. The function returns one line per managed object, with its trigger status:

schema_name table_name trigger_status public demo_painting created public demo_trees already exists public demo_nogeom geom column not found public missing_table table not found public demo_signs not requested

For each table, the created trigger is equivalent to:

CREATE TRIGGER trg_calculate_managed_object_references
BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF geom
ON public.demo_painting
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE PROCEDURE road_graph.calculate_managed_object_references();

docs.title: Update rules
docs.text:
When the user merges the data from the editing session, every impacted object is automatically updated based on the rule chosen by the administrator:

  • Point objects are often not moved, but their references must be updated, e.g. a road sign.
  • (Multi)linestring objects must often follow the changes: the start and end points are kept and only the nodes in between are edited, e.g. a painting roadwork.

The algorithm Update managed objects from the road graph can also be run manually on a given layer, with the following parameters:

  • Update policy: Update geometries or Update references,
  • Update geometries - Preserve start & end points when updating line geometries: No or Yes.

docs.title: Example: impacts of a graph modification
docs.text:
The road D613 has two business objects:

  • a tree, in the table demo_trees with the update policy references, located at PR 43 + 450.53 m,
  • a safety barrier, in the table demo_safety_barriers with the update policy geometry, from PR 43 + 120 m to PR 45 + 18 m.

The road is realigned between the marker 43 and the tree: in an editing session, a vertex of the edge is moved 40 m away from the road axis. The edge, and therefore the road, becomes 46.71 m longer (from 563.30 m to 610.01 m).

When the editing session is merged, the two objects are updated according to their policy:

Object Update policy Before the merge After the merge Tree references PR 43 + 450.53 m PR 43 + 497.24 m: the tree has not moved, but it is now 46.71 m further from the marker 43 Safety barrier geometry PR 43 + 120 m to PR 45 + 18 m, 1,843.31 m long Same references. The geometry is calculated again and follows the new shape of the road: 1,889.57 m long
  • For the tree, a real object on the ground, the geometry is right and the references are updated.
  • For the safety barrier, the references are kept: its start and end points stay at the same places, since the markers have not moved, and the geometry between them follows the realigned road.

The updated objects are listed in the column last_updated_objects_ids of the managed_objects layer, and are displayed by the layer vm_managed_objects (see below).

docs.title: Last updated objects
docs.text:
The layer vm_managed_objects shows, for each managed table, the objects updated by the last merge of an editing session, as a 10m buffer around them. It is useful to have a quick look at the impacted objects.

This layer is a materialized view based on the view road_graph.v_managed_objects, which can be slow to compute. It is refreshed automatically at the end of the merge of an editing session. To refresh it manually, for example after running the algorithm Update managed objects from the road graph, use:

REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY road_graph.vm_managed_objects;

docs.title: Processing algorithms
docs.text:
The plugin adds the provider RoadNetwork to the QGIS Processing toolbox (menu Processing / Toolbox). Most of the algorithms are also available with the buttons of the toolbar and panels.

Group Algorithm Usage Configuration Configure plugin Choose the PostgreSQL connection of the project Structure Create database structure Install the schema road_graph in the database Structure Upgrade database structure Upgrade the schema after a plugin upgrade Administration Create database local interface Create the QGIS administration project Editing Import data from template Fill an empty road graph from edges and markers layers Editing Clone data to a new editing session Copy the data of an editing session area into the sandbox Editing Merge editing session data Merge the sandbox data into the production data Editing Update managed objects from the road graph Calculate the references from the geometries, or the geometries from the references, of a layer

All the algorithms have a parameter PostgreSQL connection to the database: by default, the connection chosen with the algorithm Configure plugin.

docs.title: Configure plugin
docs.text: Choose the PostgreSQL connection used by the current QGIS project. It must be run before the other algorithms. See Configure the plugin.

docs.title: Create database structure
docs.text: Install the schema road_graph, with its tables, views and functions, and the editing schema road_graph_editing. See Create the database structure.

docs.title: Upgrade database structure
docs.text: Upgrade the database structure to the version of the plugin, after a plugin upgrade. The administration panel shows if an upgrade is needed. See Upgrade database structure.

docs.title: Create database local interface
docs.text: Create a QGIS administration project with all the layers, styles, labels and actions. See Create your database local interface and Administration project.

docs.title: Import data from template
docs.text: Fill an empty road graph from an edges layer and a markers layer. The roads, nodes, edges and markers are created, and the references of the edges are calculated. See Import the road graph.

docs.title: Clone data to a new editing session
docs.text:
Copy the production data located inside the last editing session polygon with the status created into the editing schema road_graph_editing, the sandbox. The status of the session becomes cloned.

Also available with the toolbar button Clone data to the editing sandbox and with the action Create editing session of the editing_sessions layer.

The algorithm refuses to run if:

  • the editing_sessions layer is in editing mode: save the changes and stop the editing beforehand,
  • an editing session with the status edited has not been merged or dropped yet,
  • there is no editing session with the status created: draw the editing session polygon beforehand.

See Road graph editing.

docs.title: Merge editing session data
docs.text:
Merge the data of the editing session with the status edited into the production schema road_graph, update the managed objects impacted by the changes, then empty the sandbox and delete the merged editing session.

Also available with the toolbar button Merge editing sandbox data.

The algorithm refuses to run if the editing_sessions layer cannot be found or is in editing mode, or if there is no editing session with the status edited.

See Road graph editing.

docs.title: Update managed objects from the road graph
docs.text:
Update the references or the geometries of the features of a vector layer from the road graph. The layer can be a PostgreSQL table of the database, or any other vector layer, for example a GeoPackage layer.

Parameters:

  • Input vector layer: a point or (multi)linestring layer,
  • Update policy:
    • Update references: the references of each feature are calculated from its geometry,
    • Update geometries: the geometry of each feature is calculated from its references,
  • Update geometries - Preserve start & end points when updating line geometries: No or Yes,
  • Output layer: the layer created with the updated features.

The input layer must have the reference fields corresponding to its geometry type:

  • point layers: road_code, marker_code, abscissa, and optionally offset, side and cumulative,
  • linestring layers: road_code, start_marker_code, start_abscissa, end_marker_code, end_abscissa, and optionally offset and side.

The algorithm supports the in-place editing of the input layer: select the layer, toggle its editing mode, then use the button Edit Features In-Place of the Processing toolbox. The features are then updated directly in the layer, and the changes can be checked before saving them.

For the tables registered in the managed_objects layer, the same updates can be done with SQL, see Calculate the references. They are also done automatically when an editing session is merged, see Update rules.

docs.title: Administration project
docs.text:
The algorithm Create database local interface creates a QGIS administration project with all the layers, styles, labels and actions needed to visualize and edit the road network.

The project contains the following groups of layers:

  • editing_sessions: the areas of the editing sessions (created, cloned, edited), see Road graph editing,
  • Editing: the layers of the editing session schema road_graph_editing,
  • Data: the production data
    • managed_objects: the list of business tables based on the road network, see Managed objects,
    • glossary_road_class and roads,
    • markers: reference points (PR) and virtual markers (PRV),
    • Topology: the nodes and edges, styled by road class,
  • baselayers: the background maps.

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
The plugin adds the toolbar Road Network to QGIS:

Button Action Get references under the cursor Activates the map tool showing the references of the clicked point, see below. Shortcut: CTRL+SHIFT+K. Clone data to the editing sandbox Runs the algorithm Clone data to a new editing session, see Road graph editing Merge editing sandbox data Runs the algorithm Merge editing session data, see Road graph editing Show/hide the tools dock Shows or hides the panel RoadNetwork tools Show/hide the administration dock Shows or hides the panel RoadNetwork (administration)

docs.title: Menu
docs.text: The menu Plugins / RoadNetwork contains the actions Show/hide the tools dock, Show/hide the administration dock, and Open online help, which opens this documentation.

docs.title: Administration panel
docs.text:
The panel RoadNetwork is used by the administrator to install and configure the database:

  • the group Information shows the PostgreSQL connection used by the project, the versions of the plugin and of the database structure, and checks that they match. If the database structure is older than the plugin, it asks to run the algorithm Upgrade database structure,
  • the group Install and configure runs the algorithms Configure plugin, Create database structure, Create database local interface and Upgrade database structure,
  • the group Import runs the algorithm Import data from template.

See Processing algorithms for the description of these algorithms.

docs.title: Tools panel
docs.text:
The panel RoadNetwork tools shows the references of a point, and allows to find a point from references:

  • the group Localisation concerns the production data (schema road_graph),
  • the group Localisation (editing) concerns the data of the current editing session (schema road_graph_editing): during an editing session, the references can be different from the production ones,
  • the group Options contains the checkbox Get references on hover ?, which updates the references when the mouse moves over the map, see below.

Each Localisation group contains the fields Road, Marker, Abscissa, Cumulative, Offset and Side (left or right), filled with the references of the point clicked or hovered on the map.

To find a point from references, type the road, the marker, the abscissa and, optionally, the offset and the side, then click on Find or press Enter: the map is centered on the corresponding point, which flashes.

docs.title: Quick search
docs.text:
The QGIS locator search bar (CTRL+K) can be used to search a road or a position on a road. No prefix is needed: the RoadNetwork results are displayed in the RoadNetwork group.

Type the road code and, optionally, the marker code, the abscissa, the offset and the side, separated by spaces:

  • D40: highlights the whole road,
  • D40 1 151: centers the map on the point D40 PR 1 + 151m,
  • D40 1 151 3 left: same point, with an offset of 3m on the left side.

docs.title: Get references on map click
docs.text: The tool Get references under the cursor shows the references of the point under the mouse: road code, marker, abscissa, offset and side. It can be toggled with the plugin toolbar button or with the shortcut CTRL+SHIFT+K. Hovering over the map is supported.

docs.title: Layer actions
docs.text:
Some layers of the project have actions, run by the RoadNetwork plugin, which must be installed and activated:

Layer Action Usage editing_sessions Create editing session Create a new editing session editing_sessions Display edited data Highlight the objects modified in the session editing_sessions Drop editing session Delete the session and its data edges copie Finalize the roundabout Clean a roundabout digitized as a circle

They are used when the user would like to modify the Road graph. See the corresponding documentation.

To run an action on a feature, use the Identify Features tool and right-click on the feature in the map, or use the Run Feature Action tool of the Attributes toolbar.

The Python code of these actions is stored in the plugin: the actions of the project only call it, for example plugins['roadnetwork'].run_action('drop_editing_session', ...).
